minutes.headline: Sewer Commission pushes a state loan application for a Sunset Ave sewer extension, with Pratt Street added if residents back it
minutes.summary: The commission discussed the State Revolving Fund project evaluation form for a Sunset Avenue sewer extension, with Pratt Street included pending two-thirds resident support. It also covered Highfield Village, the Lancaster extension, the Lunenburg Village 40B increase, grease trap enforcement, the Fitchburg IMA and the contract operator's reports. A sewer credit for a new-lawn watering bill was moved and voted.

votes.motion: Give a sewer credit to a customer billed for watering a new lawn, and set notice that credits will stop in future.

budget_items.topic: Sunset Ave sewer extension, State Revolving Fund loan
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission is applying for a state loan, not a grant, through a project evaluation form due Thursday at noon.

budget_items.topic: Grinder pump costs in the PEF costing
budget_items.what_was_said: Grinder pumps and house pipes are to be removed from the costing because the homeowner owns them and the loan covers only public ownership.

budget_items.topic: Short-term town borrowing for engineering and design
budget_items.what_was_said: The town treasurer said short-term money would not be an issue and would start after Town Meeting.
Fees rose July 1 and an inflow fee began July 30; counsel is asked which date locks a rate.
A credit was moved for a customer whose usage jumped well above her history.

decisions.decision: Chair to have the engineer remove grinder pumps and house lines from the project evaluation form; members agreed without a vote.
Highfield Village tabled until plans arrive.
Commission will start enforcing grease trap reporting; staff to prepare a list of commercial properties and check with the Board of Health.
A workshop with the building and plumbing inspectors on grease trap review was proposed and favoured.
Staff to look at folding a new-lawn watering credit into the pool policy; notices to go out in spring.
Next meeting set for September 10 at the DPW at 7:00.

what_happened.line: The commission is applying for a State Revolving Fund loan, not a grant, for a Sunset Avenue sewer extension, with Pratt Street included pending resident support.
Members agreed without a vote that the engineer should remove grinder pumps and house lines from the project evaluation form, since homeowners own them.
The commission will start enforcing grease trap reporting; staff are to prepare a list of commercial properties and check with the Board of Health.
A sewer credit was moved and voted for a customer billed for watering a new lawn, with notice that such credits will stop; the vote outcome was not audible.
Highfield Village was tabled until plans arrive, and the question of which date locks a connection fee rate was referred to counsel.

why_it_matters: The loan application decides how the Sunset Avenue and Pratt Street extensions are financed, and a loan is repaid, so it bears on sewer rates and on the town budget, mostly taxes, for years.
Homeowners on the extension would own their grinder pumps and house lines, so those costs fall outside the loan and on them.
Stricter grease trap enforcement and the end of watering credits affect what commercial properties and sewer customers may be asked to do or pay.
